title: Finite-height faithfully flat valuation extension to a separable closure
statement: Let $V$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-weil-field], meaning $V\subseteq K$ and for every $a\in K^\times$ at least one of $a,a^{-1}$ belongs to $V$. Suppose the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain. Let $K^s/K$ be a separable closure, meaning an algebraic separable extension whose field has no nontrivial finite separable extension [def-kun-separably-closed]. There exists a valuation ring $V^s\subseteq K^s$ with fraction field $K^s$, $V^s\cap K=V$, and maximal ideal contracting to the maximal ideal of $V$, such that $V^s$ has the same height as $V$ and $V\to V^s$ is faithfully flat. Here height is the number of strict inclusions in the prime-ideal chain, and faithfully flat means that tensoring modules with $V^s$ is exact and reflects zero modules. Consequently the singleton $\operatorname{Spec}V^s\to\operatorname{Spec}V$ is an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering].

source.place: Valuation extension as in Temkin Section 2.1; Stacks Tag 0ASH (more-algebra-lemma-inequality-general) gives torsion value-group quotient for algebraic extensions and hence equal height; Tag 0539 (more-algebra-lemma-valuation-ring-torsion-free-flat) and Tag 00HR (algebra-lemma-local-flat-ff) give faithful flatness of the dominating inclusion.
